documents.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
documents.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte

documents.title: Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
documents.abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A, SKIL, IFNG, and B4GALT1. In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecul

documents.title: Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.
documents.abstract: Urolithins are polyphenolic compounds produced by gut microbiota from dietary ellagitannins and ellagic acid, with urolithin A being the most bioactive and associated with a range of pharmaceutical activities like anti-aging and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite these benefits, the number of known urolithin A-producing bacteria and their corresponding enzymes is very limited. In this study, we combined conventional sequence-based homology search with structural modeling to identify novel bacteria potentially harboring 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases, primarily characterized in the Enterocloster

documents.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
documents.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba

documents.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
documents.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s

documents.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
documents.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en

documents.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.
documents.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted
documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.
documents.abstract: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations generate potential of mean force (PMF) curves that integrate the energy of molecular interactions along a defined pathway, offering a means to understand how PFAS interact with and pass throu
documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B

documents.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
documents.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing

documents.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.
documents.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment-protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pig
documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters

documents.title: Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.
documents.abstract: PFAS coatings impart strong water and oil repellency on materials, but their environmental persistence necessitates sustainable alternatives. The development of alternative chemistries is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic water and oil wettability. Here, a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulation framework was developed to predict and rationalize the intrinsic water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon for both water and oil. By systematically sampling PFAS head group types (-CHO, -COOH,

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.
documents.abstract: Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. This review treats the electrode-charging methods availablefixed and constant-charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aw

documents.title: Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.
documents.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling "photonic substituent effects." Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. Using cavity-constrained QED-DFT geometry relaxations followed by QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations of the Wheland intermediates, we confirm substantial energetic reordering and p

documents.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
documents.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.

documents.title: The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.
documents.abstract: We assess the sensitivity of time-resolved observables for characterising ultrafast nonadiabatic reaction dynamics. Using the ultrafast (<100 fs) photoisomerisation of norbornadiene as a testbed, we compare the observables for trajectory surface hopping simulations carried out at four different levels of electronic structure theory, SA-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 with (2,2) and (4,4) active spaces, resulting in four different sets of dynamics with distinct lifetimes and branching ratios. For each simulation, we calculate time-resolved photoelectron spectra, and electron- and X-ray scattering signals

documents.title: Integrating Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Data with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Protein Complex Structure Prediction.
documents.abstract: Ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) provides valuable structural information about protein shape and size through collision cross section (CCS). However, it lacks atomic level structural detail. While AlphaFold has been successful in predicting monomeric protein structure, it can struggle with modeling protein complexes. To address these limitations, we developed a method that integrates IM-MS data with AlphaFold and Rosetta to improve complex structure prediction. Our approach docks AlphaFold predicted subunits with Rosetta and selects the resulting models with a newly developed score that

documents.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
documents.abstract: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.

documents.title: LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS): A Standardized Representation Language for Lipid Membrane Systems.
documents.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations of lipid membranes lack a standardized, machine-readable representation, creating significant barriers to reproducibility, data sharing, and AI-driven analyses. Current membrane descriptions are fragmented across software-specific input files, making it difficult to reconstruct published systems or compare results among studies. Here, we introduce LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS), a line notation not a simulation tool or membrane-building program, for lipid membrane simulations that extend SMILES, BigSMILES, and CG-BigSMILES to membrane systems. LiMBS version 1.0 uses
documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference.
documents.abstract: Free energy calculations are routinely used to study molecular processes inaccessible to unbiased molecular dynamics, but their utility ultimately depends on knowing when and how much their predictions can be trusted. Uncertainty estimation is therefore essential for distinguishing genuine physical features of a free energy profile from artifacts arising from limited simulation data or inadequate sampling. Gaussian processes have emerged as a powerful framework for reconstructing free energy profiles together with predictive uncertainties. However, existing implementations typically condition
documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation.
documents.abstract: We present MARS, an open-source Python package for automated conformational ensemble generation, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation of molecular systems. Built on JAX for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation, MARS is carried out with machine-learned force fields (MLFFs), including SO3LR and MACE, with a four-phase conformational sampling workflow combining metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms. The package provides automated vibrational mode classification using Wilson B-matrix projections and functional group identification
documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Force Fields and Simulation Engines: Lessons Learned from Porting Amber ff14SB and ff19SB to GROMACS.
documents.abstract: The GROMACS molecular dynamics simulation package has historically supported a number of molecular mechanics force fields, including Amber. Force fields have evolved over time and continue to do so through refinement of existing interactions and the definition of additional ones to more faithfully match real-world experiments and higher-level quantum chemistry calculations. Although users have provided a number of conversions of newer Amber force fields over the years, the two most recent Amber protein force fields, ff14SB and ff19SB, had not previously been officially ported to GROMACS. A tec
documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Orf virus early genes ORFV113 and ORFV114 are individually dispensable for replication in vitro but required for full virulence in vivo.
documents.abstract: Orf is a highly contagious zoonotic disease caused by Orf virus (ORFV), resulting in significant economic losses to the livestock industry. ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the terminal variable region of the ORFV genome, are putative virulence-associated genes. To elucidate their biological functions, we characterized the transcription kinetics of both genes and generated single-gene deletion mutants by homologous recombination, using transfer plasmids carrying flanking homology arms and an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) reporter cassette. Lamb testis (LT) cells transfected with the

documents.title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.
documents.abstract: Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation.

documents.title: Recent Advances in High-Entropy Nanozymes: From Fabrication to Applications.
documents.abstract: Nanozymes are artificial enzymes designed to circumvent the inherent limitations of natural enzymes. They have emerged as a transformative paradigm in biomimetic catalysis. High-entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes) are nanomaterials that consist of high-entropy alloys, oxides, sulfides, and other high‑entropy compounds that exhibit enzyme-like catalytic activity. HEAzymes have recently garnered substantial attention as a next-generation nanozyme. The rapid evolution of this field has been propelled by synergistic advances in nanotechnology, biotechnology, catalysis, and computational modeling, offerin

documents.title: The evolutionary history of transporters of the plastid outer envelope of Chloroplastida- a structure-sequence comparison.
documents.abstract: Plant metabolism heavily relies on plastids, derived from once free-living organisms. However, how two distinct organisms merged into one remains currently only partially understood. Protein-mediated metabolite exchange across the double-membrane plastid envelope is essential for plant cell function. Here, we investigate the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) involved in these transport processes. The mosaic nature of the nuclear genome and the deep evolutionary distance since plastid acquisition are major challenges. To address them, we combine sequence-based analy

documents.title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design.
documents.abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: HEIWA: Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Water Attention Affects Force Field Accuracy in Structure-Based Protein Language Model ESM3.
documents.abstract: Protein language models have achieved remarkable success in structure prediction and de novo design. However, their understanding of physical interactions remains limited. For structure-based models, we hypothesize that this limitation stems from the absence of explicit solvent modeling: water mediates hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic burial, and electrostatic interactions that govern protein thermodynamics and kinetics, yet current structure-based models treat proteins as if they exist in a vacuum. Using thermophilic protein classification as a proxy task for force-field awareness, per-residue l
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.
documents.abstract: AI-driven cofolding models have become central tools for predicting protein-ligand complexes, yet it remains unclear whether the resulting structures recover the correct protein conformation or merely place the ligand plausibly within an otherwise mispredicted fold. Here, we benchmark four state-of-the-art cofolding models, AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, and Chai-1, and show that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation. As test systems, we use kinases and Class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), families whos
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
documents.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co

documents.title: Azobenzene-mediated reversible conformational switching in 9,9'-bifluorenylidene-based molecular machines.
documents.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo-BF-Azo, a visible-light-driven molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9'-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two photoswitchable tetra-ortho-fluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. By using variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy and UV-vis spectroscopy, together with computational studies, we demonstrate that irradiation at 525 nm induces Azo

documents.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
documents.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct

documents.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
documents.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con

documents.title: BioLiP3: a protein-ligand affinity database integrating curated data with LLM-enabled literature mining.
documents.abstract: Quantitative binding affinities and three-dimensional protein-ligand structures provide complementary information essential for structure-based drug discovery, yet these data remain largely disconnected across existing databases and the biomedical literature. We present BioLiP3, a major extension of BioLiP that expands quantitative affinity coverage 13-fold within its structure-centered framework for biologically relevant interactions. BioLiP3 contains 593 423 affinity records, of which 591 820 are linked to three-dimensional protein-ligand structures: 45 386 experimentally resolved PDB comple

documents.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
documents.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en

documents.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
documents.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. Mice are used in biomedical research due to their genetic similarities to humans and their utility in evaluating systemic activity and safety of therap

documents.title: DTBNet: multimodal 3D geometric perception with hierarchical attention for robust drug-target interaction and binding affinity prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) and binding affinity (DTA) constitutes a core challenge in accelerating drug discovery. While existing computational methods have made progress, most models struggle to capture critical physicochemical interactions in 3D space due to reliance on 1D sequences or 2D graph structures, and exhibit limited generalization in cold-start scenarios. This study proposes DTBNet, a unified prediction framework integrating multimodal geometric perception and hierarchical attention. The framework constructs heterogeneous embeddings combining local chemi

documents.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
documents.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).

documents.title: Targeting TLR2 to Overcome Autophagy-Dependent Chemoresistance in Gastric Cancer: Integrating Molecular Docking, Mechanistic Validation, and Therapeutic Evaluation.
documents.abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major barrier to effective treatment of gastric cancer (GC), particularly in advanced disease, where cytotoxic chemotherapy often yields limited and transient responses. The present study provides integrated computational and experimental evidence that targeting TLR2 using repurposed small-molecule inhibitors can overcome autophagy-dependent chemoresistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. A library comprising 1555 FDA-approved drugs was sourced from the DrugBank database, virtual screening was executed, and two compounds, Nilotinib (DB04868) and Lomitapide (DB08827),
documents.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

documents.title: Void-Assisted Extrinsic Charge Trapping Governs Hole Transport in Organic Semiconductors.
documents.abstract: To realize electrically pumped organic lasing, single-layer devices without organic heterointerfaces have been employed to suppress efficiency rolloff. In such architectures, on the other hand, extrinsic trap states result in trap-assisted nonradiative recombination, thereby decreasing electroluminescence efficiency. Here, we elucidate the dominant factors governing extrinsic trap formation by combining current density (J)-voltage (V) characteristics of single-layer hole-only-devices (HODs) with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 6,6'-bibenzo[d]oxazole (BZ) derivatives exhibiting high phot

documents.title: From "undruggable" to tractable: Therapeutic advances targeting Kristen rat sarcoma viral homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C)-mutant cancers and emerging resistance mechanisms.
documents.abstract: This review explains the evolution of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C) from an "undruggable" target to a manageable oncogenic driver in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While first-generation inhibitors have significantly improved patient care, the emergence of complex resistance mechanisms necessitates a shift toward precision-driven combination therapies and advanced computational drug discovery. The KRAS G12C mutation is a primary driver in approximately 8.9% of NSCLC patients, particularly smokers. The development of covalen

documents.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
documents.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
documents.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.
documents.abstract: Changes in bile acids (BAs) balance lead to various metabolic diseases, yet current treatment options targeting these changes remain severely limited. CYP8B1 (cytochrome P450, family 8, subfamily B, polypeptide 1) is a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls the synthesis of 12α-hydroxylated (12α-OH) BAs. Inhibiting CYP8B1 is an attractive therapeutic strategy for attenuating 12α-OH BA levels, remodeling the gut microbiota and thereby ameliorating metabolic diseases. CYP8B1-specific inhibitors are currently lacking due to structural similarities between the active site of CYP8B1 and other CYPs, a
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
documents.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r

documents.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
documents.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent

documents.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer under exposure to synthetic phenolic antioxidants: An integrated network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
documents.abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM

documents.title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study.
documents.abstract: Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
documents.abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.

documents.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
documents.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.

documents.title: Biocompatible nanoscale contrast agents for MRI and CT scans: current progress and clinical potential.
documents.abstract: Conventional contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) have long served as the backbone of diagnostic imaging. Yet, their well-recognized limitations, including nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and progressive gadolinium deposition with Gd-based chelates, contrast-induced nephropathy with iodinated agents, and serious hypersensitivity reactions with approved iron oxide formulations, continue to drive the search for safer alternatives.
